messages:
ashley: Starting bring-up of Pelago's LoRA on mistral-1.1-int4 (staging). We need quick-eval: dates, invoice lines, currency, and span alignment. Will run baseline int8 too.

mira: Thanks. Add tricky date formats (MM/DD/YYYY, DD MMM YY, ISO week numbers) and OCR skew cases where dashes look like slashes.

toni: Noted. Pulling pelago_dates_v1.json and pelago_lines_v2.json into pack. Target size ~120 examples, 20% OCR noisy.

ops-bot: scheduled eval job eval-499999-1 on shard-7 :gear:

jay: First int4 smoke: overall span-F1 on date extraction 88.7 vs int8 baseline 92.4. Date formats with dashes drop most. Latency med 58ms/token. Memory down 51%.

ashley: That's a 3.7 absolute F1 drop — pretty significant for legal docs. Any tokenization shift observed?

toni: Ran a token-span map diff. int8 tokenization for "2023-12-01" -> ["2023","-","12","-","01"]; int4 variant seems to favor subword merging in some cases causing different span indices after decoding. This affects span-extraction models that rely on token alignment.

mira: Two options: 1) pre-normalize dates to ISO y-m-d string (no separators) before sending; 2) patch tokenizer config to keep separators as separate tokens (riskier). Which is faster to iterate?

jay: Pre-normalization is fastest. I also propose a post-validation step: if predicted span fails regex for date, trigger int8 fallback for that request.

ashley: Re-run with pre-normalizer -> span-F1 improves to 91.9. Edge-case dashes still causing 0.3pt diff vs int8 but acceptable? Cost saving ~45%.

mira: Draft note to CS for Pelago: "Merged LoRA into mistral-1.1 int4 with date pre-normalization. Span-F1 91.9 (int8 92.4). Latency unchanged; cost down ~45%. Recommend default int4 with int8 fallback on regex-fail or low-confidence (conf < 0.8). Offer optional tokenizer patch + tiny final-layer delta train to recover parity (~2 days)."

cs-liaison: Checking with customer product team. They require <1pt regression if possible. Ask if we can run a tiny final-layer delta to recover the 0.5pt quickly.

toni: Small delta on final layer (1 epoch) might close the gap. I'll prepare a quick finetune using 5k synthetic date-paraphrase examples and try 4-hour run.

ops-bot: finetune job queued ft-499999-2 (estimated 4h) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jay: After quick delta run (results incoming) we'll re-eval and update the rollout PR.

ashley: PR prepared for canary 5% + preproc + fallback rule -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/3299

mira: Thanks all. Keep this thread for updates; please drop final metrics when available. :thumbsup:
